issues.title: Bundle: sparse perfect-HJ exact BF (E0028) + branch-free fixed 8-byte BitPacking per-value extract
issues.hypothesis: E0028 was a near-miss with no regressions. It got q07 -9.0% in the official run (-11.5/-12.9/-17.7% in the implementer's runs; it needed -13.1%), q02 -7..-22%, visible geomean -1.9% (-3.2% implementer), and hidden validation passed. Today's q07 profile shows why it helps: the lineitem scan feeds the l_suppkey=s_suppkey perfect HJ (0.24s CPU) with 18.2M rows that pass only min/max, and the HJ cuts them to 1.46M. With the slot-bitmap exact BF the scan emits about 1.46M rows. At that density (~8% < 1/4) the other lineitem columns (l_orderkey, l_extendedprice, l_discount, l_shipdate) go through the E0027 per-value BitPacking select. So in q07 the select path now carries most of the decode work, and the same is true for every BF-filtered scan (q05/q08/q09/q14/q19). The per-value extraction, BitpackingExtractValue (bitpacking.cpp:876), does memcpy(&bits, ptr, byte_count) with byte_count computed at runtime. That is a variable-length copy, usually an out-of-line memcpy call plus branches, done for every selected value. r11 measured ~26ns/value over count(*) at 5% pass, which is far above the ~1-2ns a shift-and-mask should cost. Loading a fixed 8 bytes (memcpy with a constant size of 8 compiles to one mov) removes the call. This is Part 2. It speeds up the path E0028 sends more rows into, and it gives a general gain on every sparse-select scan.
issues.plan: Part 1: re-apply E0028 exactly as described in the ledger, keeping all three of its pieces. (a) In physical_hash_join.cpp, JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters / CanUseBloomFilter (~946): let a perfect HT through when count*4 <= range+1, accept the exact BF only (TrySetExactBloomFilter must succeed), and do not set SetBuildBloomFilter. (b) Add PerfectHashJoinExecutor::FillExactBloomFilter in perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp: InsertExact(build_min widened to 64 bits + slot) for each set bit of bitmap_build_idx, or for every slot if the build is dense. (c) Add a helper PushPerfectHashJoinBloomFilters, called after FinalizeFilters when use_perfect_hash is set, in both the serial PhysicalHashJoin::Finalize path (~1282-1300) and the parallel PerfectHashJoinBuildEvent::FinishEvent (~648, after FinishBuild). Part 2: in src/storage/compression/bitpacking.cpp, BitpackingSelect FOR branch (~930-940): when the 8-byte read stays inside the segment buffer, load uint64 with memcpy(&bits, p, 8), then shift and mask. Compute a per-call safe limit from the segment handle pointer + segment.SegmentSize() (or the block size), and fall back to the existing variable-length BitpackingExtractValue only for values whose byte offset + 8 exceeds it. Hoist the mask ((1<<width)-1) and the width out of the loop. Optionally also hoist the per-value `group_pos - idx_in_block` arithmetic: block_start = group_ptr + (group_pos/32)*4*width bytes. Test correctness on an ATTACHed file db with force_compression='bitpacking' + CHECKPOINT (TEMP tables are never compressed): compare sum() of a selectively filtered BIGINT/INTEGER column at widths 1..56 against the uncompressed table. Then run the E0028 correctness queries again (negative shifted keys, RIGHT join with a NULL build row, USMALLINT key, parallel sparse build).
issues.expected_gain: q07 -12..-18%, q02 -7..-20% (from E0028). Part 2 adds a few % on the sparse-select scans in q07/q05/q08/q09/q14/q19. Visible geomean -3..-5%.
issues.generality: Part 1: any FK join against a selectively filtered dimension whose key range is <=1M (or <=4M dense) and that the perfect HJ handles: the classic star-schema case. Part 2: every scan whose non-filter BitPacking columns are decoded through a sparse selection (all BF/zone-filtered scans). Possible slowdown: sparse perfect builds whose BF does not filter, but SelectivityOptionalFilter switches those off. Part 2 has no algorithmic change.
issues.risk: Low-medium. Part 1 already passed hidden validation once. In Part 2 an out-of-bounds read at the segment end is the only hazard, and the bounds guard handles it. A wrong shift or mask would show up in the width-sweep test.

output.memory:
## Memory (gen2)

## State
- gen1 (r1-r16): accepted E0001 JoinDependent rule order (q19), E0002 contains() selectivity (q09), E0003 perfect HJ RIGHT (q13), E0005 BF first key multi-key HJ (q09), E0006 key-set range filter through compress projs (q18), E0007 exact bitmap BF, E0011 semi-join estimate, E0012 OR-of-ranges mask, E0014 FSST simple decode + substring prefilter (q13), E0016 DELIM_GET-build BF (q22 -20%). Best 1.281x.
- gen2 r1+r2: E0017/E0018 (no CM on hash-join keys) RETIRED twice: hidden validation regressed. DEAD.
- gen2 r5: E0021 = bundle of E0019 (deliminate SEMI) + E0020 (exact BF through CM offset) ACCEPTED.
- gen2 r6: E0022 exact-BF small-range floor ACCEPTED (geomean -9.9%).
- gen2 r7: E0023 ANTI deliminator ACCEPTED (q22 -22..-29%).
- gen2 r8: E0024 parallel perfect-HJ build + INNER dense <=4M ACCEPTED (q14 -7%).
- gen2 r9/r10: E0025 (exact BF to 2^27) and E0026 (+fused hashed probe) RETIRED as near-misses.
- gen2 r11: E0027 = per-value BitPacking select + E0025 tier ACCEPTED (geomean -9.0%). Best 1.676x.
- gen2 r12: E0028 sparse perfect-HJ exact BF (filled from bitmap_build_idx) RETIRED as a NEAR-MISS. Official run: q07 -9.0% (needed -13.1%), geomean -1.9%, no regressions, hidden ok. Implementer runs: q07 -11.5/-12.9/-17.7%, q02 -7..-22%. A good idea that fell short on measurement.
- gen2 r13: DISPATCHED the bundle of E0028 + a fixed 8-byte load in BitpackingExtractValue (bitpacking.cpp:876 uses a variable-length memcpy per selected value).
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run. Treat them as strong measured priors, not landed code.
- .dbe/issues.md old entries are stale or dead.

## Acceptance lessons
- Acceptance needs BOTH: some template faster beyond its noise AND a visible geomean that improves. Any template slower beyond its noise gets the issue retired.
- Bundle a near-miss with a general second mechanism that hits the SAME template (this worked in E0021 and E0027).
- If the r13 bundle fails on q07 noise again, try E0028 plus a second q02 mechanism, or drop it.

## Key finding r13: q07 plan (current best)
- HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 0.48s CPU: it builds 1.46M rows from lineitem⋈supplier (payload includes uhugeint n_name) and probes only 100k orders. The orders scan is 0.39s (15M -> 100k via BF(l_orderkey) + BF(c_custkey)). The HJ l_suppkey perfect join is 0.24s. The customer scan is 0.08s.
- HJ build cost is superlinear: 468k-row build = 0.071s (150ns/row), 1.46M = 330ns/row. Likely cache misses on the 32MB pointer table. A partitioned build would be the fix, but it is a big change. Flipping build/probe would not help (orders⋈customer is also ~1.2M).
- Scan filters already go through AdaptiveFilter (row_group.cpp:759), so filter order between BFs is adaptive. Do not propose filter reordering.

## Key finding r12: perfect HJ never pushes a BF (in the current best)
- CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:946) returns false if is_perfect_hashtable. The perfect paths are PhysicalHashJoin::Finalize ~1282-1300 (serial) and PerfectHashJoinBuildEvent::FinishEvent ~648 (parallel). The E0028 design is in the ledger.

## Key finding r11 (landed E0027): BitPacking select
- BitpackingSelect (bitpacking.cpp:886): per-value FOR extraction when sel*4 <= count. DELTA_FOR still decodes everything. Open: the 1/4 threshold is untuned; Roaring validity and ALP/Chimp have no select.
- TEMP tables are never compressed. To test compressed storage: ATTACH a file db READ_WRITE + SET force_compression + CHECKPOINT.

## Key finding r9: an exact bitmap BF probe is ~2x cheaper than a hashed BF probe

## Large perfect HA (E0009/E0013): q13 -20% real but q18 +8% beyond noise each time
- Possible cause: 22-bit per-thread tables (~64MB x 8). A retry needs range-sized tables. Unverified.

## Measured (warm JSON)
- q03: HJ l_orderkey=o_orderkey 0.34s CPU (build 1.45M orders, probe 301k), lineitem scan 0.39s, orders scan 0.13s.
- q09: lineitem scan 3.8s CPU cold; HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 1.05s warm (build 3.27M).
- q13: inner agg 2.02s CPU (15.3M rows, 1.5M groups), orders scan 1.70s (NOT LIKE), decompress proj 0.24s, RIGHT HJ 0.25s.
- q05: lineitem scan 0.93s, HJ l_orderkey 0.33s, multi-key HJ 0.15s with an unfiltered supplier build.
- No PK/UNIQUE constraints in the schema.

## How to get full operator timings
- dbe-tool sql "<q>; <q>; SET enable_profiling='json'; SET profiling_output='/home/shresth/dev/db_evolve/work/slots/slot0/.dbe/scratch_x.json'; <q>", then Grep '"operator_timing"|"operator_name"|"operator_cardinality"|Dynamic Filters|"Conditions"'. /tmp is NOT readable.
- dbe-tool profile q07.m0 works (instance names are qNN.m0). Its output is truncated near the bottom.
- Micro A/B: CREATE TEMP VIEW a/b, then `from a; from b;` alternated 4x in one call. The first run is ~3x slower.
- Bash: only dbe-tool; no ls, no pipes, no cd compound commands.

## Measurement lessons
- Alternate A/B/A/B. Do NOT wrap in count(*) (it changes the plan).
- Bench noise ±10-20% per template. Thresholds: q16 ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%, q14 ~5.1%, q05 ~20.3%, q04 ~20%, q07 ~13.1%.

## Profile snapshot (r13): q18 548, q13 530, q09 430, q05 204, q07 189, q16 186, q03 176, q08 156, q04 147, q17 115, q14 115, q22 103, q19 92, q02 61. Geomean 176.1.

## Dead / exhausted
- CM join-key removal, HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ (8M range), hashed BF through CM offset, q13 eager aggregation, fused hashed BF probe.
- q18: the 15M-group agg dominates (exhausted).

## Next candidates
1. (dispatched r13) E0028 + BitPacking fixed-load bundle.
2. Tune the BitPacking select threshold (1/4); add select for DELTA_FOR (decode only up to the last selected row) and for ALP.
3. q13 agg 127ns/row: range-sized perfect HA, allocated so q18 is not hit.
4. Large HJ builds (q03/q07/q09 1.4-3.3M rows, 230-330ns/row): radix-partitioned or cache-friendlier pointer-table insert. Big change; check join_hashtable.cpp InsertHashesLoop first.
5. MARK delim joins (IN/EXISTS in OR) via the deliminator.

## Codebase facts
- CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization*. Rule order: src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp.
- Deliminator: src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp. Join filters: JoinFilterPushdownOptimizer::GenerateJoinFilters; build_side_has_filter = IsFiltering(children[1]) (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:210,334).
- Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp (CanDoPerfectHashJoin :66, BuildPerfectHashTable :144, FinishBuild :262). Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp. FSST: src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp. BF: src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp; exact tiers in physical_hash_join.cpp TrySetExactBloomFilter ~972; exact BF fill in join_hashtable.cpp ~731-769 (InsertFirstKeyIntoExactBloomFilter); hashed BF inserted in JoinHashTable::InsertHashes :771.
- BitPacking: src/storage/compression/bitpacking.cpp (ScanPartial ~770, Select :886).
- Budget is tight (~$4/session): read memory, the ledger tail and the profile head, profile 1-2 queries, then dispatch.
